newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks seen rising 3,000 tonnes - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks seen rising 3,000 tonnes - trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper stocks are expected to show a modest rise of around 3,000 tonnes later on Tuesday, Singapore-based metal traders said.
"It'll (the copper stocks figure) will probably rise about 3,000 tonnes," one trader at a European firm said.
The comments came after earlier forecasts from traders in New York that the move in LME stocks could range between a 2,000 tonne drop and a rise of 9,000 tonnes.
LME aluminium stocks are seen staying stable, traders said.
"I do not see a big change in the figures," said a dealer with a U.S company.
Most traders said they were unsure of the volume of copper stocks moving to Singapore as a gradual return from the New Year holiday period has left available information scarce.

Others were expecting only a small rise in LME copper inventories in the city-state, citing the winding down of Chinese activities as traders prepare for the 15-day Lunar New Year holiday period in February.
The amount of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse rose to 40,050 tonnes on Friday, up just 300 tonnes from the previous January 7 report.

Three month LME copper copper was quoted by regional dealers at around $2,263/68 a tonne at 0230 GMT on Tuesday, little moved from its late trade in London on Monday. Traders expect the red metal to hover between $2,260-$2,280 in the LME session.
Three month LME aluminium was indicated at $1,621/25 a tonne, up from its close in London on Monday at $1,607.
"If trade breaks the $1,620-$1,630 resistance (in aluminium), levels could move as high as $1,670-$1,690," said a Singapore- based trader.
"Levels are likely to consolidate today," he said.
